project.title: Narrative Scene Tracker
project.summary: A stateless AI backend that turns narrative observations into structured scene and character memory, returning the updated snapshot with a detailed execution trace.

preview.description: An early illustration pairs a narrative scene with structured character details to explain the scene-memory concept.

blocks.body:
## Carry scene continuity between narrative observations

Scene Tracker provides structured memory for SceneGen. A caller supplies its current scene snapshot, one narrative observation, bounded supporting evidence, and optional context. The backend returns an updated snapshot describing the scene, characters, and physical interactions, together with the processing record.

The maintained API is stateless: the caller owns persistence and decides which returned snapshot to keep. Bootstrap initializes an opening scene, while tracking applies a new observation through the same request and response contract.

blocks.code:
flowchart TB
  Input["Caller-owned snapshot + observation"] --> Operation["Bootstrap or track"]
  Operation --> Workers["Configured worker pipeline"]
  Workers --> Tools["Validated state tools"]
  Tools --> Commit["Commit successful transactions"]
  Commit --> Output["Updated snapshot + changes + trace"]
  Output --> Caller["Caller retains scene memory"]
blocks.description: The backend transforms a supplied snapshot; storage and conversation ownership remain with the caller.

blocks.body:
## Turn model findings into controlled state changes

Configured workers use constrained tools to propose changes. Failed steps discard their transactional mutations. Successful character workers can commit independently, merging only the top-level fields each instance changed.

The reported changes describe the canonical difference in the committed snapshot. Supporting evidence and invocation context guide processing without being copied into persistent scene memory.

## Make the complete execution inspectable

The processing endpoint streams ordered NDJSON events for the request, steps, workers, models, and tool calls. A terminal completed or failed event tells the caller whether the stream produced a valid result; an interrupted stream is incomplete.

Diagnostics describe rejected candidates, recoveries, degraded outcomes, and failures with machine-readable codes and locations. The retained trace records model rounds, tool feedback, timing, and whether each transaction committed.

## Bound orchestration across service boundaries

One deadline covers the processing request, including worker fan-outs and provider calls. Caller disconnection cancels the processing task. Correlation IDs pass into downstream model requests and return in the trace.

The Model Manager adapter uses its versioned catalog to distinguish an absent model from an unavailable provider. Strict configuration, request validation, and bounded protocol repair keep unexpected model behavior visible.
